note: One entry per product page (/products/<slug>), in the founder's six-product structure (PRODUCT_DIRECTION section 8): Hubs, Feedback, Campaigns, LunchVoice for Discord, Developers, Privacy. This file feeds the page, the Products menu, the footer, the search metadata and the sitemap. Every claim must be true of the product on main today: check AGENTS.md (pricing), PRODUCT.md and docs/backend/API_CONTRACT.md before editing. Nothing planned (Pulse, missions, recaps, AI) is described as available. In planRows, a row with `key` is read from the server's entitlement map (lv_plan_limits) and is left out when the map has no value; a row with `cells` is a fact that does not vary by a limit. Cells are [Free, Starter Hub, Team Hub].

products.name: Hubs
products.line: A home for your community at lunchvoice.com/yourname.
products.title: Hubs: a home where your community decides
products.description: Give your community its own address on LunchVoice, with members, roles, pages and Campaigns. Choose who can join and what they can see.
products.h1: One address where your community asks, answers and sees what changed
products.lede: A Hub is your community's place on LunchVoice. It has its own address, colour, members and roles, and everything you ask lives there, so people always know where to go and what came of it.
audience: Clubs, teams and groups that ask their members things more than once
Community managers who already have a Discord server or a group chat and need a place to decide
Organisations that want members, roles and results in one place

points.title: You decide who gets in
points.body: Open to anyone signed in, join by approval, or invite only. A private Hub looks like it does not exist to everyone outside it.

points.title: Roles that match how you work
points.body: Give people exactly the permissions they need: run Campaigns, admit members, read results. The Owner is protected and does not use up a role.

points.title: Pages for what happens next
points.body: A Newsroom to post what changed, comments, an opt-in leaderboard, a points shop, and pages you write yourself.

points.title: A card worth sharing
points.body: Every Hub has a share card with its name, members and how to join. Paste the link into a chat and it shows up properly.

planRows.label: Your own address and Hub colour
Apply for Discover at this many members

products.fits: A Hub is a community with members, and its plan belongs to that community. (Creator plans are different: they belong to one person.) A Hub is where Campaigns run. Connect it to your Discord server to post them where people already talk, and use the API to run it from your own tools.

products.name: Feedback
products.line: Surveys, polls, ratings and open feedback. Free to start.
products.title: Feedback: free surveys, polls, ratings and open feedback
products.description: Ask with a survey, a poll, a rating or open feedback. Quick Surveys are free: share a link, a QR code or a six-character code and read anonymous totals.
products.h1: Ask a question today and have answers by this afternoon
products.lede: Feedback is every way of asking on LunchVoice: a survey with several questions, a quick poll, a rating, or an open box for comments. A Quick Survey is the free version. You do not need a Hub to use it.
audience: Anyone with one thing to ask a group this week
Event hosts, teachers and team leads who want answers on phones, with no app to install
People who need honest answers and so need them to be anonymous

points.title: Four ways to ask
points.body: A survey for several questions, a poll for one quick choice, a rating for a score, and open feedback for comments. Questions can be ratings, single or multiple choice, yes or no, or short text.

points.title: Three ways in
points.body: Share a link, print the QR code, or read out the six-character code. A link survey can also let guests answer without an account.

points.title: Anonymous or by name
points.body: You choose before you publish. On an anonymous survey you see totals only, and nobody, including you, can link an answer to a person.

points.title: Start from a template
points.body: Event feedback, a team pulse, a club vote and more. Every question in a template can be edited before you publish.

planRows.label: Surveys active at once in a Hub
Link, QR code and six-character code

products.fits: Writing surveys on your own? Creator Plus ($5/month) and Creator Pro ($15/month) are per-person plans that open with billing. Linked Questions, custom branding and Trends are coming soon. When the same people keep answering, give them a Hub and run your feedback as Campaigns: scheduled, aimed at your members, and followed by what you did about it.

products.name: Campaigns
products.line: Feedback run inside your Hub: who, when, and the results.
products.title: Campaigns: scheduled surveys and polls for your members
products.description: Run surveys, polls, ratings and open feedback inside your Hub. Schedule them, choose who answers, and close them when you have what you need.
products.h1: Ask your members properly: scheduled, aimed and closed on time
products.lede: A Campaign is feedback running in a Hub. It has an audience, a beginning and an end. Draft it, schedule it, open it to your members, and close it when you have what you need.
audience: Hub owners who ask their members on a schedule
Groups that need a vote or a survey to open and close at set times
Organisers who need a Hub for a few weeks, not a monthly plan

points.title: A clear lifecycle
points.body: Draft, scheduled, open, closed. Questions can change while it is a draft and lock once it is published, so everyone answers the same thing.

points.title: The right people
points.body: Open a Campaign to every member, or on an identified Campaign to the roles you pick. Anonymous Campaigns stay open to all members so a small role cannot give someone away.

points.title: Templates for each plan
points.body: Start from a template made for what your plan is for, then edit anything.

points.title: Only for a few weeks?
points.body: A Campaign pass gives you Hub features for a set time, starting at two weeks, with no subscription.

planRows.label: Of those, surveys active at once
Schedule an opening and closing time

products.fits: Campaigns live in a Hub and use the same feedback types as a Quick Survey. Post one to Discord with a command, or create and publish it through the API.

products.name: LunchVoice for Discord
products.line: Discord is where your community talks. Decide here, post there.
products.title: LunchVoice for Discord: polls and surveys in your server
products.description: Connect a Discord server to your Hub, post Campaigns with one command, and give roles to members. Anonymous surveys are always answered in LunchVoice.
products.h1: Discord is where your community talks. LunchVoice is where it decides.
products.lede: If your community lives on Discord, keep it there. Connect your server to your Hub, post a Campaign into a channel, and let people answer without hunting for a link.
audience: Server owners and moderators who run votes and feedback for their community
Communities that want a record of what was asked and decided, outside the chat scroll
Hubs whose members are already on Discord

points.title: Connect in two steps
points.body: A server admin runs /lunchvoice connect with your Hub's address, and a Hub manager confirms the link it posts. That is the whole setup.

points.title: Post with one command
points.body: /lunchvoice post puts a Campaign card with an Answer button into the channel. Or turn on auto-post and every Campaign you publish appears on its own.

points.title: Anonymous stays anonymous
points.body: Discord can see who clicks a button, so anonymous Campaigns always open in LunchVoice. Identified polls can be answered right in Discord.

points.title: Roles from real facts
points.body: Give a Discord role to people who are members of your Hub. It applies only to people who linked their account and agreed to it.

planRows.label: Connect a server to your Hub

products.fits: The bot is an official LunchVoice integration built on Discord's public tools. It posts Campaigns from your Hub; your Hub stays the place where results and decisions are kept.

products.name: Developers
products.line: An API and webhooks to run LunchVoice from your own tools.
products.title: LunchVoice for developers: API and webhooks
products.description: Create and publish Campaigns, make invites and read released results over a REST API. Signed webhooks tell your systems when something happens.
products.h1: Run LunchVoice from the tools you already use
products.lede: Team Hubs get API keys for their Hub. Create Campaigns from your own system, read the results that have been released, and receive a signed webhook when a Campaign opens, closes or reaches a milestone.
audience: Teams that want feedback inside a product or an internal tool
Agencies and operators who run Hubs for more than one community
Anyone who wants results in a spreadsheet or a dashboard of their own

points.title: Keys with scopes
points.body: Each key gets only what it needs: read Campaigns, write Campaigns, make invites, read results or manage webhooks. Revoke one key without touching the others.

points.title: The same privacy rules
points.body: The API returns released totals only. Withheld stays withheld, and no call returns an individual anonymous answer or who gave it.

points.title: Signed webhooks
points.body: Every delivery is signed with your endpoint's secret and retried if your server is down. The delivery log shows what was sent and when.

points.title: Nothing lost if you pause
points.body: If a Hub leaves the Team plan, keys and webhooks pause. They work again when the plan does.

products.fits: The API acts for one Hub and follows the same permissions, plan limits and privacy rules as the app. The full reference, with examples, is on the Developers page.

products.name: Privacy
products.line: Anonymous means nobody can work out who said what.
products.title: Privacy by design: anonymous answers that stay anonymous
products.description: On LunchVoice, anonymous means the creator cannot work out who answered. Small groups are withheld, and a withheld result is never shown as zero.
products.h1: Anonymous has to mean nobody can work out who said what
products.lede: People only tell the truth when they are sure it cannot be traced back to them. Privacy on LunchVoice is not a setting you find later. It is how answers are stored and how every result is shown, on every plan.
audience: Anyone asking a question people might be afraid to answer honestly
Workplaces, schools and clubs where a small group could give someone away
People answering, who deserve to know what the asker can and cannot see

points.title: Who answered and what they said are kept apart
points.body: The check that you are allowed to answer is stored separately from your answer. On an anonymous survey there is no screen, export or API call that puts them back together.

points.title: Withheld is not zero
points.body: A result that would point at one person is shown as Withheld, with the reason. You always know the difference between nobody chose this and someone is being protected.

points.title: Small groups are merged
points.body: Hidden answers are combined into one Withheld bucket, and averages that could give a group away are hidden too.

points.title: Guests stay guests
points.body: Someone who answers without an account never becomes a member, never counts toward member totals, and is labelled as unverified in results.

planRows.label: Withheld shown as its own state, never zero
Results limited to people with the results permission

products.fits: These rules are the same in the app, in exports, on Discord and in the API. The limits we know about are written down on the How it works page.
